newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS - Swiss Q1 economy posts first growth since 1995.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Swiss Q1 economy posts first growth since 1995.

text.p: Switzerland's economy grew 0.2 percent in the first three months of 1997, the first quarterly rise in two years in gross domestic product (GDP), the Federal Office for Economic Poicy said on Thursday.
Hans Sieber, the agency's director, said the latest GDP data showed the economy appeared to have steadied and was turning firmer after wavering between stagnation and decline since 1991.
"The data show that the declines appear to be over," Sieber told Reuters after the Q1 figures were released.
"We expect a gradual improvement in the second half of this year," he said.
Sieber said the latest numbers confirmed his agency's forecast of 0.5 percent annual growth for 1997, as against a drop last year of 0.7 percent based on provisional figures.
The figures showed first quarter GDP rose at an annual, seasonally-adjusted rate of 0.2 percent compared to the fourth quarter of 1996.
Versus the first quarter of 1996, GDP fell one percent.

The office also said the fourth quarter 1996 GDP fell by 1.2 percent versus the previous quarter, revised down from a previously reported unchanged reading in the fourth quarter 1996 versus the third quarter 1996.
The office said the last time quarterly GDP data showed growth was in Q1 1995, when it rose 0.9 percent.
Swiss economists had forecast the first quarter to rise 0.3 percent versus the fourth quarter, and to fall 0.3 percent versus the first quarter 1996.
